title: The Nebula's Gases
description: The gas between the stars is mostly hydrogen and helium, with a trace of everything else. Spun fast, a gas sorts itself by mass: heavier molecules drift outward, and a cascade of centrifuges multiplies the small difference each one makes. That is how deuterium is taken from hydrogen, and helium-3 from helium-4: helium-3, which fuses with deuterium into helium and a proton, with no neutrons to wear out the reactor. Jupiter's air holds it as the Sun was born. Unlocks scooping Nebular Gas, separating it, a probe into Jupiter's atmosphere, and D-He3 fusion.

puzzle.goal: Two gases whose molar masses differ by Δm spin at peripheral speed v at temperature T. Write the separation factor α of one centrifuge, with R the gas constant.
puzzle.name: Separation factor
puzzle.ask: Find α for helium-3 and helium-4 (Δm = 0.001 kg/mol) at v = @{v} m/s, T = 300 K, R = 8.314.
puzzle.method: In the spinning frame each gas settles as in gravity, with potential −½ω²r²: the Boltzmann factors differ by Δm.
